utterances.text: It does not have weapons, but in view of the situation we were in, we were the territorial Defence actually and the Territorial Defence does have weapons, but our function was more along the lines of Civil Defence, something in between, between Civil Defence and Territorial Defence. We cannot under any circumstances, however, call it an army that we had in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In 1992, prior to the conflict at the barricades, in October 1992, is it true that your brother was commander of the Territorial Defence of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many people were there in the Territorial Defence under his command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Close to 100 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You told the investigators of the Prosecution that there were 120, is that more accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are rough figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, how were these 120 people in the village organised? Was there a separate organisation for Gornji Ahmici, the central part and then the lower part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. According to the hamlets these guards were organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So that I am right when I say that Gornji Ahmici said it had its own group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How would you call central Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grabovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it is Grabovi, where the Kupreskic houses are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And Donje Ahmici had their own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Zume, where the Muslims lived close to the Croats, Santici, in the local commune of Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The Zume, were they separate or were they attached to Donje Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were under our command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now before this conflict in October, what I am interested in is was your brother Muris a commander of all the men from Zume, Donje Ahmici, Grabovi or commander of all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was commander of all men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was his second in command and who was in charge of the upper Ahmici, Gornji Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not have a second in command. I know that his deputy was Mirsad Ahmic and he did not have many deputies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did he have someone who was responsible or who was commanding in the upper Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was making the plan of all the watches, where the watches would be located.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mirsad Ahmic was his deputy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did your brother have any other assistants under his command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did, but for the most part -- it was not a real strong command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your brother was leading this weak organisation? Who was his commander, to whom did he report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the Territorial Defence headquarters in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was Sefkija Djidic commander in the Territorial Defence headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Sefkija Djidic at that time was not his commander, up until the conflict in October, but yes, he was later, but I do not know who was his commander at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But he was subordinate to the TO headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us move on to the barricade in October now. What did it consist of? How did it look specifically? I have never seen a barricade in my life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could have seen it on television. I also was never on that barricade, but they put -- they laid some mines on the road and maybe the anti-vehicle barriers and then people were out on the road, so that was the barricade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were there also some trenches around the barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no trenches. Then we dug up a couple of them overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said dug?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We dug them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you do it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, our people did, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where were these trenches located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were near this barricade, they were not right next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were they both to the left and the right of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were only on the left-hand side towards Busovaca, not on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many mines were there laid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were on the road, but there were not many.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where was the ammunition kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ammunition?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, and mines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were brought down from -- from when there was that explosion in Slemenje, somebody brought them and somebody laid them around.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But if I am not mistaken, Slemenje happened in February 1992. Where were they kept until then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not kept in any particular place. Everybody brought some with themselves. There was not one central storage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So they were kept around homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before they were kept in the houses, you mean this was in the homes in Ahmici, that is what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it was not much ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were there any mortars there or any RPGs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was one, but it was broken. There was one but it was not working and the Croats saw that. We did not have shells for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was commanding the people at the barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muris Ahmic -- you mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The barricade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The barricade was manned by four persons, Zahid Ahmic and Ermin Ahmic. There were two or three other men there, I do not know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could we say that it is correct that Zahid Ahmic was the commander of the barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that, but that was not a great command post, but yes you could say he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is it correct that Sulija Ahmic was at the barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are several Sulija Ahmics, I do not know which one. The older one or younger one?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Any Sulija Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not say that because I was not there. I know about these two men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Ramo Bilic, do you know, was he at the barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you about the two persons of whom I knew. I cannot tell you about the rest. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: After this incident with the barricade, your brother stopped being the commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What were the reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He sort of psychologically was debilitated by this torching of houses and that attack, and so psychologically I know, but I do not know if the military command ordered him to relinquish his duty. I do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the examination-in-chief, you said, "we put up a barricade in the village". Did your brother receive an order from the TO headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did receive an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: From the TO headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In this small command, did you have a radio transmitter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where was it kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the elementary school in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The night before the conflict at the barricade, were you in the school where that radio transmitter was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was not manning it, but I was around. I was near the school building in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were you able to overhear the radio traffic going back and forth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not, but the communications person was working on that. I was not listening in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were there communications with the TO headquarters from that radio transmitter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were instructions requested what to do in this situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not commander and I was not a communications person, so I cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, please, feel free to say whatever question you are unable to answer. Please tell me about these houses and stables which were torched in October of 1992. Where were they located, near the road, near the barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, near the road, all of them. Only one stable was in the upper --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: These houses have already been identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I think it was not in relationship to the barricade. We are talking about the stables that were torched in October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, all right, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, these houses and these stables were near the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but some were much farther away, those that were torched in Zume, so none of them were around the barricade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we say how many there were around the barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three houses were torched near the barricade and one or two over in Zume.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that 80 per cent of the civilians were expelled. Do you refer to the lower Ahmici or all of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of Ahmici, because the people from Gornji Ahmici were expelled to Vrhovine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know that a Croatian soldier was killed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When the incident with the barricade was over, was anything fixed and was anything repaired and who was involved in this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some construction supplies arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the municipality help, the Croats, did they help?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trust me, I just do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the negotiations after the barricade was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother Muris and Fejad went there and I know that a compromise was reached. The Croats asked that all rifles be turned over and our people said, "we will turn in four rifles" and they agreed to that. Maybe there was a political agreement reached in Vitez in higher up structures, but I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned that those four rifles belonged to the Croat military policemen. Do you know, under what circumstances was this taken away from them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had come to the barricade and were disarmed there. This was a frequent type of case. The sides were disarming each other at the barricades, but the Croats had many more barricades, and much more arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know from where these military policemen were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that they were Kordic's military policemen, so they were from Busovaca or from Vitez, I do not exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This conflict itself, from which side did the attack come, from the side of Vitez or -- that is the attack on the barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was from the Busovaca side, and from the direction of the village of Rovna, that is where the houses were torched, specifically my stable, from the south side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said when there was this battle around this barricade that Pezer was hit and that it missed you. So where were you standing and where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were shooting from different locations. That is not where it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So were you present where Pezer was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know where he was killed? Did you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was killed near the house of Hajrudin Pjanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How far is that from the barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be about 100 metres from the barricade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps we could stop here for this evening, it is already 5.45. You are not going to finish with your cross-examination tonight?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No, I will not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think it would be better to stop here, for the interpreters' sake as well. We can resume at 10.00 tomorrow morning. The court stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
